The Olive Branch, a family-owned Italian restaurant downtown, was recently named "Best New Restaurant" by the city's food critics association. Chef and owner Marco Rinaldi credits the award to his team's dedication to using fresh, locally sourced ingredients in every dish.

Since opening just eight months ago, the restaurant has built a loyal following, with many customers praising its handmade pasta and warm, welcoming atmosphere. Reservations are now recommended, especially on weekends, as the restaurant has become one of the most popular dining spots in the area.

Rinaldi says he plans to expand the menu this fall to include more seasonal dishes.

The $2.5 million project was funded through a combination of city funds and private donations. Mayor Rebecca Sung called the renovation "a wonderful investment in the community" during the reopening ceremony, which drew hundreds of residents.

Park officials say the amphitheater will host its first concert series beginning next month, with tickets available for free through the city's website.

The Riverton Hawks, the city's professional soccer team, unveiled plans this week for a new 25,000-seat stadium to replace their current aging facility. Team officials say the new stadium will include improved seating, modern concession areas, and a retractable roof to allow games during inclement weather.

Construction is expected to begin next year, with completion targeted for the 2029 season. The project will be funded through a mix of private investment and a public bond measure that voters approved last November.

Fans have expressed excitement about the plans, though some have raised concerns about increased traffic in the surrounding neighborhood.
